clue.text: One falls in crossing a stretch of water

indicators.note: the single letter drops into the middle of the river crossing, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a ford is a shallow river crossing
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles into the water while wading across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls in' puts I inside FORD. 'crossing' looks like a verb with 'One' as its subject, but it is the noun giving FORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiord, an alternative spelling of fjord, is a long narrow sea inlet between cliffs.

clue.text: Eve, wife of 26, perhaps

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the biblical Eve and a president's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 refers to 26 across, Ulysses S Grant, an American president; his wife held the official title.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve was the earliest woman in Genesis; a US president's wife holds the title used for the spouse of the head of state.

clue.text: Class system

explanation.definitionFit: An order is a rank or category in biology or society, and also an arrangement or method that keeps things in sequence.

clue.text: On good terms with the director-general outside the House

indicators.note: the initials of the official go round the outside of the phrase meaning friendly

parts.note: DG is the standard abbreviation for director-general, as at the BBC
to be well in with someone is to be on friendly terms with them

explanation.surface: A staffer cosying up to the boss of the corporation, away from Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts the D and G around WELL IN. 'House' looks like Parliament but is the definition, a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a place where people live, so a home or residence.

clue.text: Votes cast are for Eden, nonetheless

indicators.note: letters cast about are thrown into a new arrangement
read as none-less: nought, the letter O, is dropped from the word for

explanation.surface: Ballots are being cast in favour of Anthony Eden all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' is read as 'none less', so nought goes from the middle word, leaving FR before 'cast' does its work. Anthony Eden was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public ballots on a single question, so collectively they are votes.

clue.text: Carpet's value

explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is an old verb for scolding, like carpeting an employee; a rate is also a price or charge.

clue.text: People will say where the crew live

indicators.note: the clue asks how the words are spoken, so the spelling follows the pronunciation

parts.note: people are folks, and will shortens to 'll, giving folks'll

explanation.surface: Locals will tell you where the sailors are lodged.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is pronounced and often written fo'c'sle, which sounds like 'folks'll'.
explanation.definitionFit: The forecastle is the forward part of a ship below deck, traditionally the sailors' quarters.

clue.text: Find out about doctor, in principle

indicators.note: the medical degree goes inside the word for a principle

parts.note: a rule is a principle or standard
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Learning about a medic's guiding beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in principle' reads as a stock phrase, which hides the container signalled by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumble is informal British for seeing through or discovering the truth about someone.

clue.text: Prowler manages nearly to melt potassium

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
to thaw is to melt
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: Someone stalking about just about manages to dissolve a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manages' is a link word, joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nighthawk is a person who is active or roams about at night.

clue.text: Bill, a rising player

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tor is a rocky hill, a rising piece of ground

explanation.surface: A man called Bill is an up-and-coming performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like an adjective for the player, but 'a rising' is a noun, a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a performer who plays roles on stage or screen.

clue.text: Canine compiler for Pravda?

explanation.definitionFit: A red setter is an Irish breed of dog; a communist crossword compiler on the Soviet newspaper Pravda would be a Red setter.

clue.text: Force child to be heard but not seen

indicators.text: to be heard but not seen
indicators.note: inverts the saying about children: the word for a child is only spoken, not written

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Coercing a youngster to be noisy rather than quiet, reversing the old proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface twists 'children should be seen and not heard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or power, so force.

clue.text: The Thunderer gives nothing away, indisposed to provide sensation

indicators.note: with away, says a letter is surrendered from the god's name
with gives, says a letter is surrendered from the god's name

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
O is nought, nothing
ill means unwell, indisposed

explanation.surface: The Times, nicknamed the Thunderer, remains silent while feeling unwell, to create a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Thunderer' is a nickname of The Times newspaper, but here it is the god Thor; 'gives away' removes O from THOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden feeling of excitement, a sensation.

clue.text: He should be good at marbles

definitions.text: He should be good at marbles

parts.words: He should be good at marbles
parts.note: marbles reads as the children's game, but means works carved from the stone

explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor carves statues, often in marble, so marbles are his products.

clue.text: In a fit of depression, rashly spent bad old money

parts.note: to blue money is old British slang for squandering it
evil means bad or wicked
s is the abbreviation for the shilling, a pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: Feeling low, someone splurged recklessly on worthless antique currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue devils is an old expression for low spirits or melancholy.

clue.text: Where Clementine's cobbler worked, after many delays?

explanation.walkthrough: In the song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine', her shoes were enormous, so her shoemaker would have needed a very long last, the foot-shaped block cobblers use.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler shapes shoes on a last, so a big shoe needs a long one; the phrase also means finally, after a long wait.

clue.text: Coals were sorted by type

indicators.note: sorted means put in a different order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lumps of fuel were graded according to kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted by type' reads as one phrase, but 'type' alone is the definition in the printer's sense, linked by 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower case is printers' type for small letters, as against capitals.

clue.text: Singer's perch

explanation.definitionFit: A bass is the lowest male voice, and also a spiny-finned fish of the perch family.

clue.text: Chez Badger, entered first and made oneself at home

parts.note: chez means at the home of, and a badger's home is a sett
someone who led in went in at the front

explanation.surface: At the badger's house, someone went in ahead and got comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle in is to become comfortable in new surroundings.

clue.text: Beat girl first for showing the wrong letters

indicators.note: says the young woman's word comes at the front, ahead of the word for beat

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
to pelt is to beat or batter

explanation.surface: Hitting a young woman ahead of others, for displaying the wrong characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat girl' reads as a 1960s film title; 'first' moves the girl to the front, and 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspelt describes a word written with incorrect letters.

clue.text: Open entrance to companionway in the wrong direction

indicators.note: says the letters are read backwards, from right to left
the stairway's last letters are where one enters once the word is read the other way

explanation.surface: An opening leading to a ship's ladder faces the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong direction' reads companionway backwards, and 'entrance to' takes the first four letters of that backward reading: the last four of the word, NWAY, turned round. A companionway is a ship's stairway.
explanation.definitionFit: To yawn is to gape or open wide, as a chasm does.

clue.text: Use tact, like me, freely — it pays the bills

indicators.note: freely says the letters move about without constraint, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone advises using diplomacy without restraint, as they do, because it brings in money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' is a link word: the fodder is TACT LIKE ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal ticket is a person or thing relied on as a source of income.

clue.text: Express carries accepted figure

indicators.note: the verb holds the letter inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: to state is to express
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, socially acceptable usage

explanation.surface: A fast train carries a recognised personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a train, but it is the verb STATE. 'carries' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure.

clue.text: Exclude articles in cloth

parts.note: to bar is to exclude
three articles: a, the and a

explanation.surface: Banning items made of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives three grammatical articles, A + THE + A; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen fabric with a pebbled weave, used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Travel up in vehicle that's fabricated

indicators.note: the reversed verb is placed inside the word for the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Going upstairs on a vehicle that turns out to be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives OG, which 'in' places within the vehicle; 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means fake or counterfeit, invented rather than real.

clue.text: American sort of fuel producing good results

parts.note: US is short for the United States, so American

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, so the letters of the word are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A US variety of petrol that works well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of fuel' reads as a type of fuel, but sort is the anagram signal for FUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Useful means serving a purpose, beneficial in effect.

clue.text: Cobweb, for instance, is quite left out

indicators.note: says the letter for left is removed from the word for quite

parts.note: fairly means quite, moderately

explanation.surface: A spider's web is rather neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobweb is a fairy in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare names one of Titania's attendant sprites Cobweb, so it is an example of a magical sprite.

clue.text: Hit hard, cracked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: cracked and nuts both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Struck violently and broken into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to knock someone senseless with a blow.

clue.text: Gift for Ulysses

explanation.definitionFit: A grant is a sum given, a donation; Ulysses S Grant was the 18th US president.

clue.text: Spindrift is about to happen

explanation.definitionFit: Spindrift is spray blown along by the gale; something imminent is said to be stirring as if carried on a breeze.

clue.text: Writer and inventor, we're told

indicators.note: means the inventor's name is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: George Stephenson built the Rocket locomotive

explanation.surface: Naming an author and an engineer by report.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island; George Stephenson was a railway pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish novelist and poet.

clue.text: Hear about an attempt to deceive

parts.note: a judge hears a case, which is to try it
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Listening to talk of a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the courtroom sense, to judge a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-on is British slang for a cheeky attempt to fool someone.
